Math / Area

Area Calculator

Calculate area for a rectangle, triangle, circle, or trapezoid from the dimensions each shape requires. The selected formula and squared unit keep the geometry clear, whether checking a room plan or a classroom exercise. Rectangle area is lw; triangle area is bh/2; circle area is πr²; trapezoid area is (a+b)h/2 for parallel sides a and b. For the trapezoid, h is the perpendicular distance between its parallel sides, not the sloping side. Use matching length units throughout so the result is consistently in square metres, square centimetres, or another squared unit.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter shape, length / radius / parallel side a, width / height / parallel side b and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How area is calculated

Rectangle area is lw; triangle area is bh/2; circle area is πr²; trapezoid area is (a+b)h/2 for parallel sides a and b. For the trapezoid, h is the perpendicular distance between its parallel sides, not the sloping side. Use matching length units throughout so the result is consistently in square metres, square centimetres, or another squared unit. A 4 m by 6 m rectangle has area 24 m².

Rectangle lw; triangle bh/2; circle πr²; trapezoid (a+b)h/2.
A worked example

A 4 m by 6 m rectangle has area 24 m².

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Do I enter a circle’s diameter?

Enter its radius.

Why is area measured in square units?

Multiplying two lengths creates a squared unit such as cm².
